headline: Target: traffic up 5% and comparable sales up 5.6% — the turnaround is showing in the numbers
takeaway: Net sales grew 7.1% and comparable sales 5.6%, driven almost entirely by a 5.0% rise in customer traffic. EPS of $2.65 includes $0.50 of tariff refunds; excluding them, adjusted earnings still rose 21%. Target raised its full-year sales outlook and said November is tracking in line with plan.
results: Target reported third-quarter net sales of $27.1 billion, up 7.1%. Comparable sales grew 5.6%, with store comparable sales up 4.6% and digital up 9.8%. Comparable traffic — the number of transactions — rose 5.0%, which means nearly all the growth came from more visits rather than higher prices.

GAAP and adjusted EPS were both $2.65, against adjusted EPS of $1.78 a year ago and a consensus of about $2.08. The figure includes $301 million of pre-tax tariff refunds, worth $0.50 per share. Excluding them, adjusted EPS was about $2.15, up 21% and still ahead of the consensus.

Growth was broad: nearly 27% in the toys, sports and entertainment category the company calls Fun 101, more than 9% in beauty and nearly 7% in food and beverage. Non-merchandise sales — advertising, card profit-sharing, memberships and the marketplace — grew nearly 20%.
mgmt: Chief executive Michael Fiddelke said the results reflect progress on the company’s strategic priorities, centred on what he called its blend of style, design and value, and that the company’s investments are building on one another to create momentum.

Target raised its full-year net sales growth outlook to around 6%, one percentage point above the prior range. It expects an operating margin of around 6.2%, including about 1.1 points from tariff refunds, and GAAP and adjusted EPS of $10.65 to $11.40, which includes about $2.14 of tariff refund benefits recognised so far this year.

The company said net sales grew in all three months, strongest during the back-to-school season, and that November sales to date are in line with guidance and accelerating from October. It is going into the holidays with more than 8,000 new gift items, over half of them exclusive.
view: Traffic is the number that matters in retail, because it cannot be manufactured by raising prices, and Target’s 5.0% is the best evidence so far that its turnaround is real. For two years the company lost visits to Walmart and to off-price chains while its discretionary categories — home, apparel, toys — sat on the wrong side of a consumer spending on essentials. A quarter in which nearly all of a 5.6% comparable increase comes from more customers walking in is a change in direction, not a blip.

The guidance needs unpicking, because the tariff refunds make it look better than the business is. The full-year EPS range of $10.65 to $11.40 includes $2.14 of refunds; without them the range is about $8.50 to $9.25. And the operating margin of 6.2% includes 1.1 points of refunds, so the underlying margin is nearer 5.1%. That is below where Target ran before its difficulties and tells you the sales recovery is being bought with investment — in price, in stores and in the new merchandise the company keeps emphasising.

That trade-off is the right one at this stage. A retailer recovering lost customers should accept a lower margin to win them back, and the margin can be rebuilt once the traffic is secure. The mix helps: non-merchandise revenue growing nearly 20% is the same advertising-and-membership engine that has transformed Walmart’s profitability, at an earlier stage. Roundel, Target’s advertising business, earns far more per dollar than selling goods.

The fair criticism is that this is one strong quarter against an easy comparison — a year ago Target’s traffic was falling. The two-year figures the company cites show acceleration, which is the right way to look at it, but the holiday quarter is the test. Target earns a disproportionate share of its profit in November and December, and its discretionary-heavy mix makes it more exposed than Walmart to how freely people spend on gifts. The comment that November is in line and accelerating is as much reassurance as a company can give at this point in the season.
watch: Fourth-quarter comparable traffic and the operating margin excluding tariff refunds. Traffic staying positive through the holidays confirms customers are coming back; the underlying margin shows what winning them back is costing.
